A1.justification: Both PDFs describe CS-Aligner, with matching methods and experiments. All 16 pages of v1 and 21 pages of v2, including appendices, equations, tables and embedded figures, support comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original text-to-image generation, cross-modal retrieval and ablation results in Section 4 and Appendix D.

after.justification: V2 retains those original results and adds classification, hyperparameter sensitivity and KL-divergence comparison results in Appendices D and G.

M1.justification: Both versions retain the weighted CS-divergence/InfoNCE objective, KDE estimator, unpaired-data and token-alignment extensions, and adapter/LoRA approaches. V2 adds theoretical explanations without documenting a new algorithm component or changed procedure.

E1.justification: V2 adds few-shot image classification on ImageNet, Caltech101, DTD, EuroSAT, FGVCAircraft, Food101, Flowers102, OxfordPets, StanfordCars, SUN397 and UCF101 (Appendix G). This substantially broadens task and domain coverage beyond the retained generation and retrieval evaluations.

E2.justification: V2 adds two targeted comparators: CLIP-Adapter for classification (Table 5) and KL divergence plus InfoNCE for unpaired alignment (Appendix D.2). Comparator membership in the existing generation and retrieval tables remains unchanged.

E3.justification: New protocols include ViT-B/16 classification using 16-shot subsets, lambda and kernel-width sweeps on 10,000 MSCOCO training samples, and a pairwise feature-distance diagnostic. The Gaussian example's stated standard deviations also change from (10, 0.1) to (2, 1). Existing generation and retrieval settings are retained.

E4.justification: V2 adds tests of sensitivity to both loss weighting and kernel width (Table 6), KL-based alignment stability under unpaired data (Appendix D.2), and paired-feature distances (Figure 1c). Existing adaptation, multiple-caption, unpaired-data, token-alignment and InfoNCE-only analyses remain.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run or seed counts, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. The new pairwise-distance histogram describes variation across samples, not uncertainty across experimental runs.

E6.justification: Existing benchmark tables and ablation scores are retained. V2 adds classification results averaging 80.9 versus CLIP-Adapter's 79.3, sensitivity FIDs, pairwise-distance findings and KL nonconvergence. The reparameterized Gaussian example reports KL 6.81 instead of 5194.89; however, its revised parameters and Equation 15 yield approximately 2.81.

T1.justification: V2 adds alignment–uniformity decompositions, a Taylor-based conflict argument and supporting derivations (Sections 2–3 and Appendix C), plus formal support conditions for KL versus CS divergence (Appendix D.2). It corrects the CS integral to use a common variable. Existing RKHS and prior-loss connections are retained, partly relocated.

C1.justification: Beyond v1's claim that mutual information misses distributional alignment, v2's abstract, introduction and conclusion claim that InfoNCE contains an inherent alignment–uniformity conflict and that CS-Aligner resolves it. This adds a central theoretical contribution while retaining the original alignment and downstream-task claims.

C2.justification: V2 introduces a mechanism involving cross-modal repulsion versus within-modality uniformity and expands the applicability argument against KL divergence. Appendix G newly claims broad hyperparameter robustness, although Table 6 shows substantial lambda sensitivity. The existing limitation to unCLIP-based generation remains.

D1.justification: Appendix F explicitly clarifies text-only adapter use for generation and adapters for both modalities in retrieval/classification. Appendix G documents the new classification backbone, shot setting and sensitivity subset. Existing hardware, optimization, decoder, kernel and LoRA details are retained; no new code or data access is provided.

R1.justification: V2 adds Wang and Isola's alignment–uniformity framework, a short comparison with mutual information divergence, and citations to ClipCap, SigLIP and EVA-CLIP. Most existing literature and related-work discussion remain; relocating Related Work does not itself change positioning.

P1.justification: V2 substantially reorganizes the narrative around two InfoNCE limitations, creates a separate diagnostic section and consolidates the methodology. Related Work moves after the experiments, while the formal toy example and several methodological arguments move into reorganized appendices. The abstract and introduction are extensively revised.

P2.justification: The two-column format becomes a single-column layout with wrapped tables. V2 adds Figure 1c, redraws and reorders Figure 2, merges v1 Figures 4 and 6 into Figure 4, and introduces classification and sensitivity tables. Existing appendix image examples are retained and resized.

improvement.justification: V2 preserves the main results, adds useful classification and sensitivity evidence, and corrects the CS integral definition. However, its stronger theoretical argument includes an unjustified interchange of expectation and logarithm in Appendix C. The revised toy example's KL value contradicts its formula, and Appendix G understates lambda sensitivity despite FIDs spanning 29.86–81.34. These empirical benefits and reliability problems in the new material leave the net quality direction uncertain.
